sentences.text: Probably the least important person on this meeting is being recorded.
That's exactly what I imagined.
So.

But yeah, no, I just wanted to hop on a call and kind of, it feels like, you know, there's a little more momentum now and we've had this management meeting and some requests, so just kind of wanted to regroup on process and timing and valuation, that kind of side of things, you know, as our team is kind of starting to do a bit more work.
So I don't know if you had any context just in terms of any of those topics and, you know, I can get into some specific questions.
Yeah.
So timing.
So for us, this is obviously a fairly extended conversation with Zipf.
We're very keen to move things forward.
We have about three or four other conversations that are ongoing and they're in various stages.
There is one other big holding company that would be exciting, but to be honest, the Zif Davis conversation is the most exciting.
So obviously we can be patient.
But equally, we're about eight, nine months into the process and we would like to get an offer on the table so we can start working towards closing it.
So I guess the question can come straight back at you and like, you know, do you have a feel for what the next month or so would look like in a process with, with zip?
I mean, how fast do you guys normally move?
Yeah, sorry, go ahead.
I was just going to say on the, on the other question, in terms of valuation, I think we came to this with good intentions, giving them a high valuation.

Our managing director, David Satsumi is in San Francisco and software valuations are obviously massive there, but it seems the market has responded that it's too high where we originally positioned it.
So I've spoken to them about what you suggested on the last call that we had, where you said 12 to 14, I think was the range of EBITDA multiples.
So I've prepared them for something that's more realistic.
Okay.
I, I'm not sure If I said 12 to 14.
Maybe I, maybe I did.
I think, I think one thing on valuation is just, especially right now with where the markets are, you know, and where we're trading at.
It's definitely difficult I think right now to get some internal support for double digit EBITDA multiples.
That said, I mean, that's not a black and white case.
Well, this is, it is, it is a software play, part of it.
But I do appreciate that some of the business is also consultancy and agency.
I'm talking about tsg, not Zif.
So.
So I would Understand if, I mean if you used various multiples for various parts of the business, it would be understandable.
These guys want to sell.
I don't know if you've had the full story, but John, one of the other founders, has had cancer and he's just looking to retire and get out of the business.
So from that point of view it's, he wants to, he wants to leave.

And Stuart is, as you can see, very ambitious and very engaged and he would still love to, to, to drive this business forward and if it was part of Zif or somewhere else that excites him, which Zif definitely does, then he's going to be happy.
So.
But we've just got these two different.
Yeah.
People that are in completely different places in their lives.

So while obviously everybody, particularly John, would like to have an enormous exit that he can retire on, the reality is whatever the business is worth to the buyer is what we're realistically going to get.
So to reiterate, you're not the only one in the running but equally you are the favorite and we understand that you can only offer what the finance.
Yeah, I think we, yeah, we haven't completely formed our view on valuation which I think is probably the biggest next step on like for us.
I think a lot of those follow ups and just understanding.

I spoke to Maureen after the management meeting and understanding the growth plan and you know, a bit more of the details behind that would help us build our own and help us get to evaluation because typically we know we look at multiples but we also build kind of a, A, P and L of what the company would look like under Ziff Davis.
And I think we're still in the learning stage of things where we don't have that view particularly completely.

I think we could definitely help with that, you know, because I mean, I don't know, obviously your focus has been around publishing and some other stuff around retail, but I think that the market is more diversified in Europe and the UK and so we can kind of see the opportunity in the US that maybe you can't see as well.
So maybe that's part of what we need to do next as well is like this is how we see the opportunity because I mean it's a massive opportunity.

What you have in the US is a market that's dominated by the sort of two, two large or enormous retailers and then below that there is probably a middle market which is unexploited in terms of this type of software and this type of marketing.
So there's a huge Opportunity for smaller networks of maybe like 100 stores or whatever.
But Ziff could easily get in there.

And because you've got the voucher business that you've already been flexing as well, that there are some areas where the combined business could really make some headway and be worth hundreds of millions.
So not to, not to say then we should inflate the valuation, but certainly the value of this business is quite big, potentially especially over the next five years.

And so if we, I mean, obviously I want to get the best valuation for my client, but if you guys recognize that it might not all be upfront, but there'll be some way that we can earn together, you know, dependent on outcomes, then obviously that's important as well.
It's not all about, you know, millions in cash up front, although that's lovely.
But it's also what could the entire business be worth to everybody over a period of time and how can they get some value out as well?
So, yeah, that makes sense.
So I think that that all makes sense and I think those follow ups will definitely help us form our view of the P and L.
And I think Maureen's out for the next two weeks.
She's kind of the key stakeholder here.
She's on holiday in Thailand.
So I think in the, you know, as you guys work through these follow ups, you know, we'll start kind of building the case internally and all of that.

And I think, you know, I think the strategic fit is there, I think, and what it comes down to a lot of processes for us is valuation and where our kind of investor committee and investment committee, like, wants to see valuation.
So I think the biggest thing for us is coming up with a view on valuation and just discussing it internally as well as with you guys to see if, you know, we're in the same ballpark.
Because I do think the, you know, the strategic fit is there.
And so I think.
Yeah, I was, I also just wanted to hop on the call to see, you know, where any other bids were or your bidders and if you had any outstanding bids just because.
Yeah, just timing.
Yeah, so.
So we don't have any, anything else on the table, but, but just on that, you know, getting to evaluation, I'm happy to work with you to get that over the line with my clients.
You know, we've got to be realistic at this point.
We've been out in the market for a long time.
We've spoken to all the big players.
Yeah.
So.
And there is obviously a fantastic fit with Ziff and so we've got to be realistic on what you guys can afford.
Again, we want the best offer, but equally, you know, you've got to give us an offer that you guys are happy to make and yeah, you can live with.
So, so let's just get that over the line together.
You know, if you need to sound a number with me before you take it into the investment committee, then I'm happy to sort of feel that out.
Yeah, I mean, if it's drastically lower than what we've got, then absolutely fine.
Just give us the ballpark and let's work with that.
Yeah, yeah, I don't want to, I don't, definitely don't have a number to share right now.
But it's just, especially with the markets right now, it's just so much uncertainty.
And so that's kind of just in other processes, you know, valuation gaps is I feel like the biggest, you know, reason that deals don't end up going through for us.
So we obviously want to cross that bridge as soon as possible to, you know, save time on both ends.
Please.
We would like to cross it as soon as possible as well.
So.
So I mean, if you can get as a ballpark number, I will get that over the line with my client if it, if it's possible.
Okay.
You know, yeah, it's just, it's too good a fit for them to miss and I'm sure there will be upside during the earn out for them to, to capitalize on.
So that really it's down to them to prove it, you know, prove that the model works within the Zif Davis business, I guess.
In terms of an earn out, is there a certain threshold of percentage wise that they want up front?
You know?
Well, we always work how much in an earn out.
We always worked at the theory of 50, 50 up front.
Okay.
But, but what, what I've seen, and we did a really good deal with Stagwell actually for another client is that there was less in cash up front.
There was some, some shares in the business for some rollover equity.
But also the earn out was very generous, but it was over a long period of time.
So I mean it was over five years that one, which I don't really like.
But, but even if it was over three years, but it was fixed to outcomes.
Yeah.
But it rewarded them very well for those outcomes, then that is good.
And if that ended up being, you know, I'm just throwing numbers around now, but just say it was like, you know, 50 million but only 20 million up front and the rest was.
Or only 10 million up front, but the rest was earn out.
Then I think the opportunity for them to get there would be.
Would be really good.
It's not just about the money up front, but obviously we need to get it right.
Like I said, we need to get John out of the business as well.
So.
Yeah, got it.
All right.
Yeah, that's helpful.
Appreciate the candidness.
So I will keep working with Steve and Maureen and as we get follow ups, feel free to send them as.
As they're completed rather than one nice package and I'll let you know, you know, where you could potentially fill in gaps and.
Sounds like a plan to me.
Yeah.
All right.
Just, I mean, again, just sort of off.
Off the record, generally speaking.
Why?
You know, you said that your deals don't always go through because of the gaps in valuation and obviously can't give us a valuation.
But I'm just saying like strategically, are you guys.
Do you guys kind of lowball stuff and see what you can get or do you do.
Because the deal.
No, I wouldn't say we, we lowball.
I think it's.
We like to value things based on.
Without the, you know, building in a bunch of synergies that are on us or a big question mark.
So I think we spend a lot of time upfront on what we're realistically going to pay versus you know, I feel like in a lot of processes people throw out numbers in an IOI and then retrade down.
Um, and so I think, you know, we're just realistic and disciplined.
I wouldn't say low ball at all.
That's not our strategy.
So.
Yeah, I mean, I think just, just because we have so much experience doing M and A.
That's why I would say like things aren't closing because.
Not because of our lack of due diligence or something, it's more of just.
Yeah, valuation.
But that doesn't mean we lowball offers.
Just to clarify.
Yeah, no, I wouldn't want to give.
Off the record as well.
Just.
Yeah, yeah, yeah.
Obviously there is going to be an expectation gap, but we've already started to address that.
So that was based on our last call where you said 12 to 14.
I can root that out for you if you mentioned it, but I think you, you remember talking about software.
Okay, yeah, just because.
Yeah, I feel like 12 to 14 is kind of a random number in my head.
So I don't know where I, when I would have specifically.
You might be freestyling.
Maybe you just got out of bed.
Maybe if it was a 6:00am meeting, but.
Okay, that makes sense.
And we'll keep working and let you know when we have any more questions.
Okay, Brilliant.
All right, look, happy to work with you, and let's get it over the line if we can.
It sounds like you guys are keen, so, you know, I think we just need to try and make the financial part fit for everybody's sake, because it's.
It's a good partnership.
Sounds good.
All right, cool.
All right, enjoy the rest of your day then.
Erica, nice to speak to you.
You too.

summary.overview: In the Business Development/Acquisition Discussion meeting between Erika and Andy, key topics were addressed regarding the acquisition process, specifically focusing on the ongoing discussions about Ziff Davis. Andy detailed that they are 8-9 months into the process and emphasized the need to advance towards a formal offer. Discussions around valuation indicated differing views on EBITDA multiples in the current market landscape, with Erika noting challenges in securing internal support for double-digit multiples. Both parties explored growth potential, highlighting that Ziff Davis sees significant opportunities in the U.S. middle market, while also analyzing deal structures involving upfront payments and performance-based earn-outs. The timeline for next steps was set, with Maureen, a key stakeholder at Ziff Davis, currently unavailable for follow-ups due to travel. Despite some differences in valuation expectations, both Erika and Andy expressed a commitment to bridging gaps and finding a middle ground to facilitate a strategic partnership. Action items were assigned, with Erika focusing on reinforcing the internal business case and Andy committing to provide insights on market opportunities.
summary.short_summary: In a Business Development meeting, Erika and Andy discussed the ongoing acquisition process of Ziff Davis, which is currently 8-9 months underway. They emphasized the urgency to move towards a formal offer while navigating differing views on EBITDA multiples. Erika highlighted challenges in gaining internal support for double-digit multiples, while both recognized Ziff Davis's growth potential in the U.S. middle market. They also explored deal structures, considering upfront payments and performance-based earn-outs. A timeline for next steps was established, although follow-ups were delayed due to Maureen's unavailability. Despite valuation differences, both Erika and Andy showed dedication to bridging gaps for a successful partnership, with assigned action items focusing on reinforcing the internal business case and providing market insights.
